title: HC surge playbook: capacity-price coupling and sensitivity
summary: One-page working sheet: ties headcount surge options to capacity price pressure scenarios. Purpose is to give finance + ops a quick decision matrix and cost delta table for rapid response windows (7–90 day). Not a final budget — operational playbook + triggers for Q3–Q4 2027.
content:
Goal and scope:
- Purpose: present a compact scenario matrix that maps GPU/spot-price moves and token-demand shocks to short-term headcount surge options and recommended pricing levers.
- Audience: CFO, head of finance, SRE lead, capacity planning PM, and commercial leads.
- Horizon: immediate tactical (next 90 days) with a 12-month rolling view for budget impact.

Assumptions (working):
- Baseline monthly token volume (M tokens): 1,200M in Nov-2026 baseline, 1,500M midpoint forecast for Q2-2027.
- Unit infra cost per 1k tokens (baseline): $0.0018. Downside stress: +60% infra cost (to $0.0029). Upside efficiency (batching/quant improvements): -30% ($0.00126).
- Price elasticity: assume -0.6 elasticity for enterprise self-serve (i.e., 1% price increase -> 0.6% drop in volume), -1.2 for low-touch SMB.
- Hiring lead times: infra/SRE hires 6–10 weeks to be productive for reactive ops; applied-ml/model infra hires 10–14 weeks.

Scenario matrix (short descriptions):
- Scenario A (Base): token growth +10% q/q, infra costs stable. No immediate hires beyond planned.
- Scenario B (Surge): sudden +40% token demand (30 day window), spot GPU prices +45%. Unit cost spikes to baseline * 1.45.
- Scenario C (Price compression): customers push back on list price; commercial team requests 10% discount cohort; combined with moderate demand dip (-8%).
- Scenario D (Efficiency recovery): model upgrades and batching yield -25% unit cost within 60 days, enabling lower price without margin loss.

Headcount surge options (practical bundles):
- Option 1: Minimal ops tilt (2 SRE contractors for 3 months, 1 capacity planner) — +$85k/mo runrate in labor but reduces incident mean-time by ~22% and unlocks immediate autoscale tuning. Hires: 2 contractor SREs (60% utilization), 1 0.5 FTE capacity PM.
- Option 2: Rapid infra scale-up (hire 3 SRE full-time + 1 release Eng) — incremental fully-burdened cost ~$140k/mo; reduces cost-per-token by enabling reserved GPU mix and more aggressive batching. Lead time: 8 weeks.
- Option 3: Model & compiler push (2 applied ML, 1 infra engineer) — cost ~$195k/mo; expected unit cost delta: -18% within 10 weeks. High upfront time-to-impact.
- Option 4: Commercial containment (2 customer success reps + 1 solutions engineer) — cost ~$95k/mo; aimed at retaining at-risk customers when prices shift. Improves churn by estimated 1.4 p.p. in stress window.

Pricing sensitivity quick table (excerpt):
Columns: price_change | assumed_volume_delta | net_rev_delta_over_baseline (monthly) | notes
- +10% list price | -6% volume (enterp elast -0.6) | +4.0% net rev | safe in low-compet churn cohort
- -10% list price | +12% volume (promo elasticity higher) | +1.5% net rev if unit cost stable | use to protect enterprise renewals
- price floor action: rollbacks if unit cost exceeds $0.0025/1k tokens for >14 days

Tactical triggers (7–30 day windows):
- Infra cost trigger: 7-day trailing average unit infra cost > baseline * 1.3 -> execute Option 1 + deploy burst-reserve policy; notify finance and sales.
- Demand trigger: 3-day growth > 25% relative -> enable reserved capacity routing and start Option 2 hiring pipeline.
- Customer risk trigger: top-10 customers show >12% drop in weekly usage after price increase -> deploy Option 4 and temporary targeted discounts.

12-month budget impact sketch (text table):
- Baseline Opex (run-rate): $10.8M annual infra + $8.4M labor baseline = $19.2M
- Upside (efficiency realized): infra -25% -> savings $2.7M; but requires +$1.2M labor investment to deliver = net savings $1.5M.
- Downside (sustained spot spike +40% for 3 months): incremental infra cost $1.3M over quarter; labor surge options add $0.6M if fully deployed -> total hit ~ $1.9M.

Tradeoffs and decision heuristics:
- Quick hires (Option 1) buy time for software fixes and tuning; cheap but ephemeral. Good first responder during 30-day spikes.
- Hiring for efficiency (Option 3) is mission-critical for long-term unit economics but cannot be used to cover immediate price shocks. Prioritize if strike-price (unit cost) > $0.0027 for >45 days.
- Commercial gestures (discounts + reps) should be reserved for named customer cohorts; blanket discounts can compound churn risk in price-compression scenarios.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Finance: build a live variant of this sheet in Looker/Sheets with feeds for 7-day unit cost and token volume; owner: Miguel Torres. (JIRA FIN-4215)
- Ops: pre-clear 3 contractor SREs and confirm vendor rates; owner: Sana Iyer. (JIRA OPS-4372)
- Product: finalize priority list of batching/quantization experiments that can be A/Bed in 6 weeks; owner: Priya Raman. (github.com/redwood-inference/batching-expts)
- Sales: identify top-20 highest-risk accounts if we need to run targeted discounts; owner: Evan Cho.

Notes and open questions (notes-to-self style):
- Need clearer mapping between per-route token mix and model mix; currently a blunt aggregate masks hot routes (e.g., streaming chat vs. emb-only).
- Consider building a short-lived price-simulation API that can return revenue delta for hypothetical price + promo combos based on recent elasticity cohorts.
- Check legal on promotional credit rules and tax treatment of credits before broad customer pack discounts.

Appendix (quick numbers used in sheet calculations):
- Baseline monthly tokens: 1,200M
- Avg price per 1k tokens baseline: $0.0035 (list) / effective $0.0027 net after discounts
- Infra cost baseline per 1k tokens: $0.0018
- Fully-burdened SRE cost per head (monthly): $18k; applied-ml per head: $22k; contractor SRE (bench rate): $12k

Draft housekeeping: this is intentionally compact and has rough estimates. Use the linked JIRA/Confluence pages for deeper backing models. If we get a spike this quarter, run the "Surge" checklist in ops-runbook and escalate to finance for temporary credit lines.

-- Jordan

(End of sheet)
